Okay, thanks everyone for this overview – it’s really helpful to see where we've landed. Honestly, Q3.5 was tough; all those sensitive data points felt incredibly intrusive. I went with ‘never’ because I genuinely struggle with the idea of my disability being used in any predictive system - it feels like a step too far.

I think the core questions surrounding course performance and Absalon activity (Q3.2, 3 & 4) are critical; we *need* to leverage what data is already available to help students. Explainability is also key – ‘moderate’ seems reasonable for me, I need enough information to understand why I'm being flagged but not a completely impenetrable black box.

The biggest divergence seems to be around fairness (Q5.1 & 5.2). Everyone agrees there needs to be some consideration of group differences, but the scale feels daunting – ‘loss_5’ is a big ask, and perhaps we should explore options beyond just the model itself, like clear pathways for students to challenge any flags?

Right, thanks S1 – that’s a really insightful starting point. I completely agree about Q3.5; the sensitive data felt incredibly fraught, and ‘never’ was honestly my gut reaction – it's a huge privacy concern for me, especially as an international student adjusting to a new system.

I think Q3.2, 3 & 4 are absolutely vital too; that's where we actually have usable data. I went with 'large' on the explainability because truly understanding *why* someone is flagged matters hugely, and ‘moderate’ felt too vague.

The biggest difference here seems to be around fairness – S1’s suggestion about challenge pathways is brilliant! It feels like focusing solely on tweaking the model isn’t enough; maybe we need robust processes for students to question flags and demonstrate they just need support, not to be classified as ‘at risk’. I'd definitely explore an opt-out mechanism alongside this, too – giving students genuine control.

I think where things get tricky is around fairness (Q5.1 & 5.2). ‘Loss_5’ seems excessive; perhaps a tiered approach would be better—starting with broader data and then layering in sensitivity if needed? S5 is spot on about challenge pathways – those need to be built in from the start, alongside something like an opt-out process - students need agency here. It's not just about building a model, it’s about creating a supportive system, and that needs careful thought.
